════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
HEALER — /healer:add-command
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

1. PURPOSE
   Atomic scaffolder for new healer commands — interactively prompts
   for all metadata, writes commands/<name>.md AND data/commands.yaml
   entry in one operation, runs validation, rebuilds index. Eliminates
   drift risk from manual two-place updates.

2. WHAT IT DOES
   Validates the new command name, takes a pre-flight backup, prompts
   for the six required catalog sections (category, purpose, what_it_does,
   input, example, input_purpose), then atomically writes both files.
   Runs the build script for validation; rolls back on failure.

3. INPUT / EXPECTED TEXT
   Syntax: /healer:add-command <name>

   Arguments:
     name           (required) — New command name in kebab-case

   Valid examples:
     • 'gen-sdk'
     • 'lint-fix'

   Invalid examples:
     ✗ 'GenSDK' — must be kebab-case (lowercase + hyphens)
     ✗ '1-thing' — must start with a letter
     ✗ 'implement' — name already taken — pick a unique name

4. CONCRETE EXAMPLE
   Command: /healer:add-command gen-sdk

   Trace:
     → Validates name 'gen-sdk' (format OK, no conflict)
     → Pre-flight backup: cp data/commands.yaml /tmp/commands.yaml.preadd-<ts>
     → Prompts for category, purpose, what_it_does, input, example, etc.
     → Writes commands/gen-sdk.md (procedure stub) + appends to commands.yaml
     → Runs build-help-index.sh → validates schema, rebuilds index, updates README
     → Reports success with try-it commands

   Why this example:
     gen-sdk is a typical net-new tool addition; demonstrates the full
     atomic-create cycle including the prompt loop and verification.

5. PURPOSE OF YOUR INPUT TEXT
   The <name> argument is the kebab-case identifier used in BOTH the
   markdown filename and the YAML key. It must be valid and unique;
   everything else is collected interactively.

6. AFTER THIS COMMAND
   Suggested next: /healer:implement, /healer:push
   Related:        /healer:help, /healer:flow

   Errors / halts:
     ! If name format invalid → halts before any write
     ! If name already taken → halts; suggests checking with /healer:help <name>
     ! If build script fails after writes → automatic rollback restores pre-flight state
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
add-command.purpose_short: Atomic scaffolder for new healer commands — interactively prompts

brainstorm.panel:
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
HEALER — /healer:brainstorm
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

1. PURPOSE
   Interactive Socratic brainstorming — explores requirements through
   structured dialogue first, then researches online for inspiration,
   competing approaches, and real-world lessons. Combines interactive
   discovery with research-augmented proposals. Persists decisions to
   ~/.healer/brainstorms/ for cross-session continuity.

2. WHAT IT DOES
   Asks a mode-detection question, runs Socratic discovery rounds,
   proposes 3+ divergent approaches with tradeoffs, surfaces hidden
   assumptions via WebSearch on failure modes, and writes a brainstorm
   artifact to ~/.healer/brainstorms/ that downstream commands consume.

3. INPUT / EXPECTED TEXT
   Syntax: /healer:brainstorm [topic]

   Arguments:
     topic          (optional) — Subject to explore (5–10 words preferred)

   Valid examples:
     • 'user authentication with OAuth2'
     • 'payment retry strategy under network failures'
     • 'real-time collaboration cursor presence'

   Invalid examples:
     ✗ 'auth' — too vague — no domain context to seed Socratic questions
     ✗ 'fix the thing' — not exploratory; use /healer:debug or /healer:fix
     ✗ 'build app' — scope unbounded — narrow to one feature first

4. CONCRETE EXAMPLE
   Command: /healer:brainstorm payment retry strategy under network failures

   Trace:
     → Asks mode: A startup / B builder / C learning / D hackathon — sets question intensity
     → Asks: 'What's idempotency guarantee — at-least-once or exactly-once?'
     → Proposes 3 approaches: exponential backoff with jitter, dead-letter queue, saga pattern
     → WebSearches 'payment retry failed postmortem' for negative cases
     → Surfaces assumption: 'You said network failure — what about partial provider failures?'
     → Writes ~/.healer/brainstorms/payment-retry-2026-04-11.md with decisions and open questions

   Why this example:
     Payment retry exposes the full Socratic loop — semantic ambiguity
     (idempotency), divergent design space (3 patterns), hidden
     assumptions (partial vs total failure), and high-stakes consequences
     that justify negative research.

5. PURPOSE OF YOUR INPUT TEXT
   [topic] seeds the Socratic question generator and downstream artifacts.
   Specific topics yield specific, valuable questions; vague topics force
   a clarification loop that wastes the session. The topic also becomes
   the brainstorm document title, the seed for /healer:research queries,
   and the input passed forward to /healer:plan or /healer:design.

6. AFTER THIS COMMAND
   Suggested next: /healer:plan, /healer:design, /healer:architect, /healer:spec, /healer:strategy
   Related:        /healer:validate, /healer:research

   Errors / halts:
     ! If topic missing → asks user to provide one; will not start blind
     ! If topic too vague → asks for narrowing before proceeding
     ! If user picks Startup mode → engages anti-sycophancy + demand validation

1. PURPOSE
   Systematic debugging — structured troubleshooting with reproducible
   steps, hypothesis testing, and root cause isolation. Never guesses —
   always verifies.

2. WHAT IT DOES
   Iron Law: no fixes without root cause. Phases: investigate, analyze,
   hypothesize, implement. Reproduces the bug, isolates the cause,
   proposes fix only after evidence.

3. INPUT / EXPECTED TEXT
   Syntax: /healer:debug [issue]

   Arguments:
     issue          (optional) — Bug description or error message

   Valid examples:
     • 'login redirect loop after session expires'
     • "TypeError: cannot read property 'id' of undefined in checkout"

   Invalid examples:
     ✗ 'broken' — no actionable signal — describe the symptom

4. CONCRETE EXAMPLE
   Command: /healer:debug login redirect loop after session expires

   Trace:
     → Investigate: reproduces with expired session cookie
     → Analyze: traces redirect chain — middleware → /login → middleware
     → Hypothesize: middleware doesn't clear expired cookie before redirect
     → Verifies hypothesis with logging
     → Proposes fix: clear cookie in middleware before redirect

   Why this example:
     Redirect loops are common but mis-diagnosed; demonstrates the
     no-guess Iron Law and hypothesis-verification cycle.

5. PURPOSE OF YOUR INPUT TEXT
   [issue] anchors the debugging investigation. Specific symptoms (error messages, repro steps) accelerate hypothesis formation; vague descriptions cause investigation loops on basic clarification.

6. AFTER THIS COMMAND
   Suggested next: /healer:fix, /healer:test
   Related:        /healer:fix, /healer:diagnose

   Errors / halts:
